theme: “Have I not loved you?”; corrupt priests; broken faith
readingInstruction: Read Malachi 1:1-2:17. This is the last prophetic book of the Old Testament, written around 430 BC. God opens with love, and then the people argue back at every point. Watch for the repeated pattern: God’s claim, the people’s question, God’s answer.
settingTheScene: Malachi’s name means “my messenger.” He writes after the temple is rebuilt and the wall is finished, in the generation of Nehemiah’s second term. The excitement of the return has faded. The sacrifices are routine and halfhearted, the priests are careless, and many have been unfaithful to their wives. The book is set up as a series of six disputes in which God makes a statement, the people ask “How?” or “What?”, and God answers.
observation: “I have loved you, says the LORD. But you say, How have you loved us?” (1:2).
“A son honors his father, and a servant his master. If then I am a father, where is my honor?” (1:6).
“When you offer blind animals in sacrifice, is that not evil?” (1:8).
“Oh that there were one among you who would shut the doors, that you might not kindle fire on my altar in vain!” (1:10).
“For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name will be great among the nations” (1:11).
“For the lips of a priest should guard knowledge, and people should seek instruction from his mouth” (2:7).
“Have we not all one Father? Has not one God created us?” (2:10).
“For the man who does not love his wife but divorces her, says the LORD, the God of Israel, covers his garment with violence” (2:16).
interpretation:
The first line gives the key to the whole book: “I have loved you.” It is a statement of fact. But the people respond with doubt: “How have you loved us?” After the return, life was hard. The land was poor, and the nation was a small province under Persia. They wondered whether God’s love was real. God answers by pointing to his choice of Jacob over Esau. He had loved them from the beginning, by electing grace.

The first rebuke is to the priests. Their worship has become an insult. They bring blind, lame, and sick animals for sacrifice, things they would not offer to their governor. “A son honors his father… If then I am a father, where is my honor?” God says he would rather have the temple doors shut than have this halfhearted worship. “I have no pleasure in you.” Worship is not about the ritual but the heart’s honor of God.

In the middle of this rebuke is a remarkable promise: “From the rising of the sun to its setting my name will be great among the nations, and in every place incense will be offered to my name.” The Gentiles will worship. The sacrifices that the priests despise will be replaced by pure offerings from all nations.

Chapter 2 is about the priests’ failure to teach. “The lips of a priest should guard knowledge.” They have turned aside from the way and caused many to stumble. God’s covenant with Levi was one of life and peace, but they have corrupted it.

Then the prophet turns to the people. They have been faithless to one another, marrying foreign wives who worship other gods and divorcing the wives of their youth. The altar of the LORD was covered with tears. “The LORD was witness between you and the wife of your youth.” God hates divorce that comes from faithlessness. The chapter ends with a weary people who have “wearied the LORD with your words.” They say, “Where is the God of justice?” They are asking the question that the whole book is about to answer.
connection: Romans 9:13 quotes “Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated” to speak about God’s electing grace. 1 Peter 2:5 calls us to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God. John 4:21-24 speaks of true worshipers who worship in spirit and truth. Ephesians 5:25: husbands, love your wives as Christ loved the church. Matthew 19:3-9 speaks of marriage and divorce. Romans 12:1: present your bodies as a living sacrifice. 1 Timothy 3:2 requires teachers to be above reproach.
application:
Ask: am I giving God my best or my leftovers, in time, money, and attention?

Hold onto “I have loved you” when you are tempted to doubt his love.

If you are married, renew your faithfulness. If you teach or lead, guard the knowledge that others depend on.
prayerPrompts: Tell God where you have doubted his love.
Confess where you give him what is blind and lame.
Ask him to teach you to give him your best.
